source_scope: Existing figure source tables only; suitable grids primary; fixed GEM2025 assets supplementary
spatial_support: Each product retains its fixed common support; no scenario-dependent future deployment
statistics: Within-model decadal means and paired differences; four equally weighted GCMs; points=GCMs, large symbol=mean, whisker=min-max; no significance claim

figures.question: Does SSP585 necessarily increase event-related net loss relative to SSP126?
figures.claim: Suitable-grid solar mean loss is lower under SSP585 (3/4 models); wind has no agreed sign (2/4).

panels.a: Wind suitable-grid decadal loss, all three SSPs
panels.b: Solar suitable-grid decadal loss, all three SSPs
panels.c: Wind paired 2050s SSP585-minus-126 loss: grid primary and fixed2025 supplementary

figures.risk: Signed losses use contemporaneous SSP-specific normal CF; lower net loss is not a general climate benefit.

figures.question: Do SSP contrasts in exposure have the same sign for wind and solar?
figures.claim: SSP585 has higher mean wind exposure and lower solar exposure; suitable-grid wind sign agrees in 3/4 models and solar in 4/4.

panels.ef: Paired 2050s SSP585-minus-126 exposure, suitable and global grid

figures.risk: Technology-specific event unions differ; exposure is cumulative duration, not frequency; not a loss result.

figures.question: Does greater exposure over time imply greater net loss, and does the response depend on SSP?
figures.claim: Under SSP585, suitable-grid wind exposure rises in 4/4 models, but net-loss change splits 2/2; fixed2025 wind shows exposure rises and loss falls in all four.

panels.ab: Suitable-grid exposure change, 2050s minus 2030s, by SSP and technology
panels.cd: Suitable-grid loss change, same periods, by SSP and technology
panels.ef: Fixed2025 joint within-model exposure and loss changes; supplementary only

figures.risk: Grid exposure and loss have different spatial weights/supports, so no event-intensity quotient or causal mediation claim.
